tool_input.content:
Incident: KubePodCrashLooping, namespace=shop, deployment=api, cluster aurora-lab (kind-aurora-lab, kubeconfig-642bee834eb69ff0).

**Root cause:** Deployment api revision 2 added `dnsPolicy: None` + explicit `dnsConfig` with `searches: [shop.svc.cluster.internal, svc.cluster.internal, cluster.internal]` and nameserver 10.96.0.10. The cluster's actual domain (confirmed via `kubectl get configmap coredns -n kube-system`, Corefile `kubernetes cluster.local ...`) is `cluster.local`, not `cluster.internal`. Because dnsPolicy was `None`, kubelet used ONLY the supplied (wrong) dnsConfig with no fallback — new pods could not resolve any in-cluster Service name (e.g. `redis`), got `[Errno -2] Name does not resolve`, and the app's startup code exits(1) after 5 failed redis connection attempts, causing CrashLoopBackOff.

This change was NOT present in the deployment's `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` annotation — it was injected via a direct patch/edit outside the normal apply flow (worth asking "who/what patches this deployment post-apply" if it recurs).

**Why this is tricky:** Old ReplicaSet pods (previous revision, no dnsConfig override, dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst) kept running fine on the SAME node, serving 200s — so this looks like "the pod is just unhealthy" rather than a DNS-domain mismatch unless you diff the full pod spec (not just image/env) between old and new ReplicaSets.

**How to apply / diagnose fast next time:**
1. `kubectl get rs -n <ns>` — compare old vs new ReplicaSet pod templates line by line (not just image), especially `dnsPolicy`/`dnsConfig`.
2. `kubectl logs <crashing-pod> --previous` — look for "Name does not resolve" / getaddrinfo errors pointing to DNS.
3. `kubectl get configmap coredns -n kube-system -o yaml` — confirm the real cluster domain (usually `cluster.local`) and compare against any custom dnsConfig searches.
4. Fix: remove the dnsPolicy:None/dnsConfig override (revert to default ClusterFirst) or correct search domain to match coredns Corefile's authoritative zone. `kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name>` is viable if a prior good revision exists.
5. Check `kubectl get endpoints <svc>` to confirm whether the bad pods are already excluded from traffic (readiness gating) — often this is a stuck/degraded rollout, not a full outage.
tool_input.description: On cluster aurora-lab, Deployment shop/api crash-looped because a rollout set dnsPolicy:None with dnsConfig.searches using 'cluster.internal' instead of the real cluster domain 'cluster.local', breaking DNS resolution of in-cluster Service names (e.g. redis) for new pods only.

thoughts.content: Found the smoking gun. Let me verify the actual cluster DNS domain to confirm the dnsConfig search domains are wrong.

Root Cause Analysis: KubePodCrashLooping — shop/api

Investigation Summary (evidence-based)

Confirmed the symptom is currently occurring:
kubectl get pods -n shop shows api-779966d57-v8d2r with STATUS=Error, RESTARTS=3(34s ago), and describe pod shows State: Waiting / Reason: CrashLoopBackOff, Last State: Terminated / Reason: Error / Exit Code: 1, restart count climbing 3→4 across polls. This is the exact alert condition, directly observed in real time.

Isolated to a single ReplicaSet (the latest rollout):
kubectl get rs -n shop showed two ReplicaSets for api:
api-f64486c4c (revision 1) — 2/2 Running, 0 restarts, serving 200 responses on /healthz and /items (confirmed via logs).
api-779966d57 (revision 2, current/latest) — 1 replica, 0 ready, crash-looping.

Both pods run the identical image (python:3.12-alpine) and identical app code (verified via configmap/api-code), so the code/image is not the differentiator.

Found the actual failure mechanism in logs:
``
redis connection failed (attempt 1/5): [Errno -2] Name does not resolve
...
giving up: redis unavailable
`
The app code (api.py) does socket.create_connection((REDIS_HOST, 6379)) at startup, retries 5x, then sys.exit(1) — matching exit code 1 and the crash loop exactly.

Found the change that caused it — diffed the two pod specs on the same node:
Old (working) pod api-f64486c4c-zt6dk: dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst, no dnsConfig override.
New (crashing) pod api-779966d57-v8d2r: dnsPolicy: None with an explicit dnsConfig:
  `yaml
  dnsConfig:
    nameservers: [10.96.0.10]
    options: [{name: ndots, value: "5"}]
    searches:
      - shop.svc.cluster.internal
      - svc.cluster.internal
      - cluster.internal
  dnsPolicy: None
  `
  Confirmed via kubectl get deployment api -o yaml that this is baked into the current deployment template (revision 2), and notably it is absent from the kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation — meaning it was injected via a direct patch/edit after the original app

Investigation complete — root cause CONFIRMED.

TL;DR: Deployment shop/api's latest revision (rev 2, created ~90s before investigation) added dnsPolicy: None with a custom dnsConfig using the wrong DNS search domain (cluster.internal instead of the cluster's real cluster.local, confirmed via the CoreDNS Corefile). New pods under this revision can't resolve the redis Service name ([Errno -2] Name does not resolve in logs), the app's startup code gives up after 5 retries and sys.exit(1)s, triggering CrashLoopBackOff. The previous revision's pods (no DNS override) are unaffected and still serving traffic — so this is a stuck rollout causing reduced capacity, not a full outage (confirmed via kubectl get endpoints api showing only the healthy old pods are in rotation).

Fix (validated, requires write access — blocked in this read-only session):
kubectl rollout undo deployment/api -n shop — validated: revision 1 exists and is healthy (2/2 Running, serving 200s).
Or forward-fix: remove/correct the dnsConfig.searches to use cluster.local instead of cluster.internal.

Findings saved to org memory for future DNS-related crash-loop investigations.
